items.q: What should you remember about **Anti-self confabulation**?
items.a: **depressed patients generate elaborate negative self-narratives** that contradict objective progress (e.g., rehab improving but patient insists they're weakening).

items.q: What should you remember about **Sleep architecture collapse**?
items.a: **slow-wave → REM sequencing** disrupted; early waking despite exhaustion is a hallmark vegetative sign.

items.q: What should you remember about **Three chemical systems, one brain**?
items.a: **boosting serotonin alone rarely** fixes lethargy or anhedonia; psychiatrists often push/pull all three.

items.q: What should you remember about **Inflammation diverts tryptophan**?
items.a: **cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, CRP) shunt** tryptophan to kynurenine → quinolinic acid (pro-depressive) instead of serotonin.

items.q: What should you remember about **EPA rivals SSRIs in some trials**?
items.a: **≥1000 mg EPA/day symptom relief comparable** to prescription antidepressants in multiple double-blind studies (consult physician; don't stop meds abruptly).

items.q: What should you remember about **Creatine + SSRI synergy**?
items.a: **AJ Psychiatry 2012 RCT**: oral creatine monohydrate augmented SSRI response, especially in women with MDD.

items.q: What should you remember about **Ketamine/psilocybin mechanism**?
items.a: **not just "pep up" but** create distance from grief-laden self-narratives and enable neural circuit rewiring.

items.q: What should you remember about **Behavioral tools have a catch-22**?
items.a: **exercise/cold help norepinephrine, but** severely depressed patients often lack energy/motivation to start them.
